_meta.description: The t euphonique (also called t analogique): a -t- inserted between a verb and an inverted 3rd-person subject pronoun (il, elle, on) in interrogative or incise (parenthetical) structures, to avoid a vowel hiatus. Framed with hyphens on both sides. Fires only when the verb form's final letter is a vowel (e or a); verb forms already ending in d or t (which already give a [t] liaison sound) take no extra -t-.

trigger.condition: subject-verb inversion with a 3rd person singular pronoun (il, elle, on) in a question or incise, where the verb form ends in the vowel letter e or a
trigger.hyphenation: hyphen before and after the inserted t: <verb>-t-<pronoun>
trigger.no_insertion_when: the verb form already ends in d or t, since these already produce the [t] liaison sound on inversion (e.g. prend-il, répond-elle, part-il, dit-on)
trigger.irregular_note: vaincre and convaincre take -t- by analogy despite their 3rd person singular form ending in c (il vainc -> vainc-t-il), per BDL's explicit mention of these two verbs as an addition to the vowel rule
trigger.purpose: avoids a hiatus (meeting of two vowels: the verb's final vowel and the pronoun's initial vowel), hence 'euphonique'; 't analogique' because t is independently the verbal marker of the 3rd person singular in many paradigms (il finit, elle savait, on croit)

examples.note: future tense ends in a -> t inserted
irregular: ends in c, t inserted by analogy per BDL
no t needed: already ends in d
no t needed: already ends in d
no t needed: already ends in t
